key_insight: SLORR is a simple, stateless, architecture-preserving way to make neural network weights more compressible during training by directly regularizing them toward low rank.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical compression-friendly training add-on that avoids extra parameters and expensive SVD-heavy procedures, making it easier to integrate into existing large-model training pipelines.
method: Regularizes the original weight matrices during training instead of modifying the model architecture.
Uses GPU-friendly approximations of low-rank regularizers, with variants based on Hoyer sparsity and the nuclear norm.
Provides approximation guarantees for the forward and backward computations of the regularizers.
evidence_signal: Across ImageNet-1K and LLM pretraining experiments, SLORR improved compressibility while keeping overhead low: under 8% for vision models and under 1% on average for 135M–560M LLM pretraining.
watch_item: The approach relies on approximate regularizer computations, so implementation quality and approximation fidelity may affect the strength of the compression–accuracy trade-off.
paper_title: SLORR: Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
